description: Ask a chant search query of the estate behold serves, and get chant's answer: its read-contract search document, verbatim, with `link` (the behold view that draws it) and `drawn: false` added. ask never moves the person's tab; use show for that. On a declared workspace the document is chant workspace search's, with every member's rows as <member>/<id>; on one project or a Terraform folder it is chant search --json's. Uses the running behold serve of this project; with none, behold answers in this process. Needs chant 0.124.46 or newer. Which demo questions it answers: "what's in here?" is countBy kind with the query kind:aws_ (or empty); "how many resources does each module own, by type?" is countBy module, then countBy kind with the query narrowed to a module; "what would this change do, and why does it replace the database?" is plan with the query attr:planAction=replace and show planActions,planReplacePaths,planActionReason. Beside a chant search query, ask takes cypher (a read-only Cypher query over every member's graph and every index in one LadybugDB, behold#1027) or resource (resolve a name, id, address or cloud id, then a template). The query is chant's search grammar, unchanged (https://intentius.io/chant/cli/search/). env reads that environment live (chant search --live --env <env>); snapshot with env replays a recorded snapshot instead (chant --snapshot <ref>, such as latest); chant's --explain is always on, for the near-misses drawn. It takes no --check-live or --check-snapshot (drift is not drawn), and no --ambient, --src or --fail-on-drift. Read the capabilities tool first: it lists the capabilities a cap: term asks (cap:internet-reachable(22), ->[cap=network]), each one's meaning, parameters and rule (INTENTIUS/chant#4375).

countBy.description: Group the matches the way chant search --count-by does: kind, module or attr:<name> (behold#922). The answer is chant's groups and total; the view lights each group's cards and labels the group with its count. The query may then be empty, to count the whole estate.

cypher.description: A read-only Cypher query over the graph pane's database (behold#1027): every member's chant IR, every engine graph document (choudoufu, plunge) and every index version, in one LadybugDB. Tables: Resource(key, source, scopeKey, version, id, kind, lexicon, listedType, location, nativeId, name, address, ownership, attrs, tags, facts, observedAt) keyed <member>/<id> as chant workspace search prints it; CloudId(value, kind) with (Resource)-[:KNOWN_AS]->(CloudId), so the same object in two sources is two hops; (Resource)-[:REF {kind, viaAttr, toAttr, grain, origin, rule, relation, ambiguous}]->(Resource), origin derived for an identity match. attrs, tags and facts are JSON strings. Anything that writes (CREATE, MERGE, SET, DELETE, COPY, LOAD, CALL ...) is refused. Needs the optional peer @ladybugdb/core; without it ask refuses with the install line. Example: MATCH (a:Resource)-[:KNOWN_AS]->(c:CloudId)<-[:KNOWN_AS]-(b:Resource) WHERE a.scopeKey <> b.scopeKey RETURN a.key, b.key, c.value

env.description: The environment whose live state the view shows. Without it, the declared source.

inputs.description: With template: its inputs as a JSON object of strings ({"kind": "aws_internet_gateway"}).

params.description: With cypher: its parameters, as a JSON object ({"k": "aws_s3_bucket"} for $k). Values are strings, numbers, booleans or null.

plan.description: The plan read (behold#922): the query is answered at the plan depth (CHANT_TERRAFORM_OBSERVE=plan, chant search --live --env), and the cards carry each Terraform root's planAction, planActions, planReplacePaths and planActionReason. On a bare Terraform folder no env is needed; on a chant project pass env. Refused with snapshot. Runs terraform plan -lock=false in each root: it changes nothing, and reads every resource.

query.description: A chant search query whose matches the view lights, such as `attr:internetFacing=true`.

resource.description: Start from a resource (behold#1022): a name, an IR id, a block address or a cloud id (an ARN, an instance id, a Kubernetes UID). The answer is one node or the candidates, with the investigation templates that apply to it (chant's and the project's, each with its origin) and the project templates refused, with the file and field. Works without the LadybugDB peer.

show.description: Comma-separated attributes to carry on each row (chant search --show).

snapshot.description: With env: a recorded snapshot to show instead of a live read (latest, or a ref chant lists). Not with plan.

template.description: With resource that resolves to one node: run one of the templates resolve lists for that node, by name. They are chant's and the project's own (.chant/templates.json), each with its origin; ask with resource alone to see them and their inputs. A click in the graph pane runs the same template.

name: ask
